clue.text: Files put in the wrong order with malicious intent

indicators.note: putting things in the wrong order means rearranging the letters of the two words before it

explanation.surface: Someone deliberately misfiles documents out of spite.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the wrong order' rearranges the eight letters of FILES PUT.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting out of spite means wanting to hurt, the same as having malicious intent.

clue.text: Pet cried out, on its last legs

indicators.note: out here means wrong or disordered, so the letters of the words before it are rearranged

explanation.surface: A pet owner's animal yelped, near the end of its life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' signals that the letters of PET CRIED are shuffled.
explanation.definitionFit: Something worn out by age and near collapse is idiomatically said to be on its last legs.

clue.text: From a service angle is careless in dress

parts.note: the RAF, Royal Air Force, is one of the armed services
to angle is to fish with rod and line

explanation.surface: Someone from an armed services background looks sloppily turned out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'angle' looks like a noun for a point of view, but it is the verb meaning to go fishing.
explanation.definitionFit: A rakish, unconventional look includes a cheerfully untidy way of wearing clothes.

clue.text: Publicity in place of helpful suggestions

parts.note: an ad, short for advertisement, is a piece of publicity
vice is Latin used in English for 'in place of', as in vice-captain

explanation.surface: Advertising is offered where useful tips should be.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in place of' looks like the link joining two parts, but it supplies the Latin word VICE.
explanation.definitionFit: Counsel offered to someone is a set of recommendations meant to help them.

clue.text: Top car manufacturer who takes prize

indicators.note: a manufacturer makes something new, so the letters of the words before are made into a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: A leading carmaker scoops an award.
explanation.walkthrough: 'manufacturer' signals that the letters of TOP CAR are remade; 'who takes prize' means one who seizes a ship or person, not one who wins an award.
explanation.definitionFit: A prize was once a ship seized at sea, and the one who seizes it is its taker.

clue.text: Suiting the seasons?

parts.note: suiting is suit cloth, and a speckled black-and-white cloth is named after the two commonest table seasonings

explanation.surface: Clothes that are right for spring, summer, autumn and winter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'seasons' reads as times of year, but it means the condiments used to season food, and 'Suiting' is cloth for suits.
explanation.definitionFit: A fabric with flecks of dark and light is named after the two condiments it resembles.

clue.text: Style of architecture that may be dropped

definitions.meaning: a late English Gothic style known for strong vertical lines
in geometry one drops a right-angled line from a point onto another line

explanation.surface: An architectural style someone might abandon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dropped' suggests abandoned, but in geometry a line at right angles is said to be dropped from a point.
explanation.definitionFit: The English Gothic style of about 1350 to 1530 is named for its vertical tracery, and a line at right angles to another is called by the same term.

clue.text: Considered the matter closed?

parts.note: read normally it means believed a matter was finished; it also describes having pondered something at length

explanation.surface: Someone believed an issue had been settled.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase means pondered at length, but taken literally it means believed something was finished.
explanation.definitionFit: To ponder something carefully is to mull it, and the same phrase literally says one believed it finished.

clue.text: Depression after an attack, perhaps

parts.note: reads like low spirits after an assault, but means a hollow in the ground left by a bomb or shell

explanation.surface: Someone feels low after being assaulted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Depression' suggests low spirits, but here it is a hollow in the ground made by a bombardment.
explanation.definitionFit: A bowl-shaped hollow is blasted out of the ground by an exploding shell or bomb.

clue.text: False story about ringleader produces bad feeling

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the story is placed around the other piece

parts.note: fiction is made-up narrative, a story that is not true
the leader, or first letter, of the word ring is R

explanation.surface: A lie told about the head of a gang causes resentment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ringleader' looks like a gang boss, but it gives the leading letter of 'ring'.
explanation.definitionFit: Conflict or animosity between people is likened to the rubbing of surfaces against each other.

clue.text: Priest quite absorbed in his religion

indicators.note: quite absorbed in means wholly swallowed up within the words that follow, so a run of letters is concealed there

explanation.surface: A clergyman is utterly engrossed in his faith.
explanation.walkthrough: 'quite absorbed in' tells you the priest's name lies wholly inside 'his religion'.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Old Testament he was the priest at Shiloh who raised the boy Samuel.

clue.text: Reinforce complaint that's raised

parts.note: beef is slang for a complaint or grievance
raised means up, lifted high

explanation.surface: Strengthen a grievance that has been brought up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'complaint' sounds like an ailment, but it is the slang word for a grumble.
explanation.definitionFit: To strengthen or bolster something is to add muscle to it, idiomatically.

clue.text: See great changes in economy travel

indicators.note: changes signals that the letters of the words before it are rearranged

explanation.surface: Notice big differences in budget-class trips.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changes' rearranges the letters of SEE GREAT.
explanation.definitionFit: The cheapest accommodation on a passenger ship, historically near the rudder gear, was the budget class.

clue.text: Some of the musicians get the bird

indicators.note: some of means only part of the words that follow is taken, as a run of letters within them

explanation.surface: A band's performers are booed off stage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some of' takes letters straddling 'the musicians'; 'get the bird' suggests being jeered, a red herring.
explanation.definitionFit: A large flightless Australian runner is a kind of feathered animal.

clue.text: Lavish praise

parts.note: read as an instruction to heap compliments on someone, the whole clue is a verb phrase

explanation.surface: Extravagant compliments.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lavish praise' reads like a noun phrase, but it is a command: heap praise on someone.
explanation.definitionFit: To flatter excessively or worship is to heap compliments on someone.

clue.text: He gets red if a stranger addresses him

definitions.text: He gets red if a stranger addresses him

parts.words: He gets red if a stranger addresses him
parts.note: his familiar short name, with red added, becomes the full formal first name a stranger would use

explanation.surface: A man blushes when someone he does not know speaks to him.
explanation.walkthrough: The blushing is a red herring: add RED to the short name and you get the formal name Alfred, which a stranger would use.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the familiar short form of the first name Alfred, which a stranger would use instead.

clue.text: Learned English with Trudie, perhaps

indicators.note: perhaps signals that the letters of the name before it may be arranged another way

explanation.surface: Someone studied the English language alongside a friend called Trudie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Learned' looks like a past-tense verb, but it is the adjective, pronounced as two syllables; 'perhaps' rearranges TRUDIE.
explanation.definitionFit: A scholarly, well-read person is described as having great learning.

clue.text: Hot-rod driving is completely absorbing

definitions.meaning: a rivet is a metal pin hammered in while red hot, so driving such a hot rod is fixing it in
so gripping that one cannot look away

explanation.surface: Racing a souped-up car is utterly gripping.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hot-rod' suggests a souped-up car, but it is a heated metal pin hammered home by a construction worker.
explanation.definitionFit: Hammering in metal fastening pins is the trade sense, and an enthralling spectacle holds attention as if fastened.

clue.text: Separate-that's abundantly clear

definitions.meaning: separate means individual, apart from the others
abundantly clear means plainly evident, unmistakable

explanation.surface: Something set apart is obviously so.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both individually different from others and sharply evident to the senses.

clue.text: Planet rising in temperature

definitions.meaning: the innermost planet of the solar system
the liquid metal in a thermometer climbs as things get warmer

explanation.surface: A heavenly body climbs as the heat goes up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' suggests a planet coming up over the horizon, but it is the column in a thermometer.
explanation.definitionFit: The planet nearest the Sun shares a name with the liquid metal that climbs a thermometer as heat increases.

clue.text: Possible secret of not having to pay

indicators.note: possible signals one possible arrangement of the letters of the words that follow

explanation.surface: A conceivable trick for avoiding the bill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Possible' rearranges the letters of SECRET OF.
explanation.definitionFit: Getting away without penalty comes from an old word for a tax, so it means escaping payment.

clue.text: This religious belief is held by our opponents

indicators.note: held by means contained inside the other piece

parts.note: them, as opposed to us, means the other side or opponents

explanation.surface: Our rivals subscribe to this faith.
explanation.walkthrough: 'held by' puts IS inside THEM, the classic 'us and them' sense of the other side.
explanation.definitionFit: Belief in the existence of a god or gods is a religious conviction.

clue.text: When students may collect on the streets

definitions.text: When students may collect on the streets

parts.words: When students may collect on the streets
parts.note: suggests a crowd of protesting students, but means a day when British students raise money for charity in public

explanation.surface: An occasion for students to gather for a street demonstration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'collect' suggests gathering in a crowd, but means collecting charity money; in Britain, students hold an annual fundraising day of stunts and street collections.
explanation.definitionFit: In British universities, a day of charity fundraising by students involves collecting money in the streets.

clue.text: They're paid for it on board after six

indicators.note: after places this piece following the numeral

parts.note: VI is six in Roman numerals

indicators.note: on, with board, signals the word it is placed inside the ship abbreviation

parts.note: on board a ship conventionally means inside SS, the abbreviation for steamship
taken as written

explanation.surface: Crew members are paid for something aboard ship after six o'clock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on board' puts IT inside SS, steamship; 'paid' is the idiom of paying a call, not wages.
explanation.definitionFit: One pays a call, so calls on people are things that are paid.

clue.text: About to swallow duck eggs

indicators.note: to swallow means to take something inside, so one piece goes into the other

parts.note: re is a common word meaning about or concerning
a duck is a score of nothing in cricket, so it gives O

explanation.surface: A bird is about to gulp down a clutch of eggs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'duck' looks like the bird, but it is the cricket score of zero, O.
explanation.definitionFit: Fish spawn, a mass of tiny fish eggs, is eaten as a delicacy.

clue.text: Being so one may react rashly with unusual ill-grace

definitions.text: Being so one may react rashly

indicators.note: unusual signals that the letters of the hyphenated word after it come out in a different order

explanation.surface: Someone acts hastily and rudely in a bad-tempered way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rashly' suggests hastily, but refers to an itchy rash; 'unusual' rearranges ILL-GRACE.
explanation.definitionFit: A person sensitive to a substance may come out in spots or hives on contact.

clue.text: Take things the wrong way

parts.note: sounds like misunderstanding remarks, but means taking possessions wrongfully

explanation.surface: Someone misreads everything said to them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Take things the wrong way' sounds like being touchy, but means taking goods dishonestly.
explanation.definitionFit: To steal is to take others' property wrongfully.

clue.text: Its staff run a meals-on-wheels service

definitions.text: Its staff run a meals-on-wheels service

parts.words: Its staff run a meals-on-wheels service
parts.note: meals on wheels suggests delivering food to the housebound, but describes dining while a train moves

explanation.surface: A team operating a food delivery scheme for elderly people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'meals-on-wheels' is a British scheme delivering hot food to the elderly, but here the wheels are a train's.
explanation.definitionFit: A railway carriage where passengers are served meals as the train travels.
